text:
ara: quick one — onboarding reported a weird billing mixup: our CLI was inferring org from git remote for sample apps and that inference beat explicit REDWOOD_ORG env in some cases. short thread.

sam: whoa, inferring from git remote? how did that happen?

ara: sample-app startup does a `git remote get-url origin` heuristic to suggest project/org. someone added a convenience mapping so `examples/quickstart` would auto-select org. but the CLI later merged that suggestion into session metadata and it ended up being authoritative for calls.

toni: repro steps:
```bash
cd examples/quickstart
git remote add origin git@github.com:org-suspect/repo.git
export REDWOOD_ORG=org-desired
redwood start # CLI suggests org-suspect and writes session with org-suspect
redwood generate --project proj-1 --prompt "hi"
# request billed to org-suspect
```

infra-bot: created RW-9012 "git-infer-org-overrides-explicit-env" (assigned: sam)

sam: Ack. This is bad DX — explicit env should always win. Also inferring agent behavior must be opt-in and never persist as authoritative without consent.

ara: impact: a new team had production sandbox billing go to an unrelated org. luckily low charges but confusing and a trust issue.

docs: proposal: add a note in quickstart and examples: "We may suggest an org from git remote; to accept use `--use-inferred-org` or run `redwood auth accept-organize`". Also add `redwood auth preview-session` to show what session will contain before persisting.

toni: suggested fixes:
- Precedence rule: CLI flag > env var > explicit SDK param > user-accepted inferred metadata > session cache > keychain. Make inferred data require explicit `--accept` flag.
- Change startup flow: if inference differs from REDWOOD_ORG/REDWOOD_PROJECT, show a one-line prompt and do not persist unless `--yes` given.
- Add `redwood auth preview-session` to print session JSON without writing.

sam: security/rotation angle: ephemeral tokens rotated by infra expired mid-run and our retry/backoff logic treated 401 like transient and retried forever, effectively creating a hot loop hitting auth endpoints. We need clearer handling: 401 from token should trigger immediate refresh (with jittered backoff) and a finite retry window.

ara: example change: on 401 do at most 3 immediate reauth attempts then escalate to interactive warning in CLI or emit `auth.refresh_needed` telemetry for SDKs. For long-running workers provide `client.on('auth.expires_soon', handler)` hook.

toni: add sample code in Node and Go to show reload pattern (SIGHUP/SIGUSR1) and use `client.reloadCredentials()` API.

docs: will add a troubleshooting item: "If example app picks wrong org, check git remote inference and run `redwood auth preview-session`. To avoid surprises set REDWOOD_ORG explicitly or use `--use-inferred-org` when creating session."

sam: I'll open a PR to remove auto-persist of inferred org, add `preview-session`, and implement the 401->refresh finite retry behavior. tagging @eng-devex @platform.

ara: adding a small e2e: 1) set env different from git remote, 2) start app with `--dry-run`, 3) rotate token mid-flight and assert client refreshes and telemetry fired. estimate 1.5 dev days.

toni: thanks — also request QA to validate behavior in JS/py/go SDKs to ensure parity.

ara: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
